name: Rooster One
author: Oxford Metadata Ltd

sections.description:
One plugin instead of dozens. 581 tools, and they agree with each other.

Rooster One does the work that would otherwise take dozens of separate plugins, and it does it from one place, on one set of numbers.

One plugin means one licence, one update, one place to ask, and one thing for WordPress to load on every request instead of dozens.

What is actually in it: a full SEO engine that can take over from Yoast or AIOSEO, importing what they hold first. Product recommendations built from your real sales. Role, wholesale and tiered pricing. Meta, Google Ads, GA4 and TikTok measurement, sent server-side so an ad blocker cannot silence it. Sixteen couriers with vouchers, labels, tracking and daily closings. Marketplace feeds and order import for Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, Etsy, Amazon and more. Side cart, wishlist, back-in-stock waitlist, quote requests for catalogue shops, swatches, trust badges. Popups and scheduled announcements. Abandoned-cart recovery, email and web push campaigns, audiences. Surveys, competitions and events. Invoices, packing slips and credit notes. A GDPR consent banner with a cookie scanner. The EU withdrawal button that Directive 2023/2673 now requires. And an AI assistant that answers from your own catalogue rather than making things up.

That is 581 tools, each with a written description of what it is for.

Why one plugin rather than dozens

Because separate plugins cannot see what the others know, so they disagree, and each one works the same thing out again while your customer waits.

Rooster One measures your whole business on a schedule instead: every product, page, customer, order and session, written into flat tables. The SEO engine, the recommendations, the audiences, the ad ROI report and the AI assistant all read those same tables. That is why they agree, and why the plugin gets faster as you switch more of it on: the heavy work happened before the request arrived. The trade-off is timing: a figure is only as new as its last run.

And it is one plugin to load, not dozens

WordPress loads every active plugin on every request, whether that request needs it or not; a site carrying a hundred of them pays that toll a hundred times before any useful work happens. Rooster One is one plugin, and the parts you have not switched on register nothing. On Pro, a separate lightweight runtime serves the storefront, so your customer’s page load carries the code that draws the page and not the code that runs the shop.

Everything is off by default. It installs beside your current SEO plugin, pixel manager and consent tool and changes nothing until you switch a piece on.

Rooster One runs on your own server. Everything it ever sends to an outside service, and what triggers it, is listed under “What does Rooster One send to an outside service, and when?” in the FAQ below.

The free version is a complete product, not a demo: 775 of the 1,302 screens, tools and actions are in it. Pro adds the operational half and the separate front-end runtime plugin.

Who builds it

Rooster One is built by Oxford Metadata Ltd, approved under Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program for security work; the plugin’s bot filtering, form captcha, proof-of-consent log and login hardening come out of that discipline. The AI features run on Anthropic Claude and Voyage AI embeddings.

It reads your site for what it is

  • Shop — sales and add-to-carts are the measure.
  • Catalogue — products published but not sold; engagement is the measure.
  • Content — no WooCommerce; visits, engagement and forms are the measure.

Auto-detected, overridable in one click. Scoring, cornerstones and applicable signals all follow from it.

You can find all of it

Ctrl+K reaches every page and each of the 581 tools inside them. All Features lists every one, with pinnable favourites, and prints the figure for your own install, since the page count depends on which modules apply to your shop.

What gets measured

Computed on a schedule, stored flat. Everything below reads these.

  • Product vitals — velocity, out-of-stock history, price history, basket role, returns, and a 0–100 demand score.
  • Content vitals — reach, engagement, freshness and a content-demand score for every post, page and custom type.
  • Customer vitals — an omnichannel profile: purchases, affinities, lifecycle stage, survey answers, return risk.
  • Session and attribution rollups — engagement joined to conversion on one session id, with landing page, campaign and five UTMs.
  • Effective prices — every price rule resolved ahead of time into one row per product per audience.

The features

AI chat & semantic search

  • Chat widget on Anthropic Claude, grounded in your catalogue — only real, in-stock items with exact links.
  • Semantic search on Voyage AI embeddings across products, posts, pages and terms.
  • A knowledge base you control, with identity guardrails so it cannot mis-describe you.
  • Chat analytics — what was asked, how it was rated, which questions found nothing, which chats ended in an order.
  • Related content on articles, guides, listings and products, from the same index, automatic or placed by block or shortcode.

SEO engine

Imports from, and can take over from, AIOSEO, Yoast or Rank Math; stays gated behind your current SEO plugin until you switch over.

  • Head, canonical, robots, Open Graph, Twitter and JSON-LD, assembled once into a cache.
  • Commerce schema from the same tables — ProductGroup + hasVariant, per-variant colour, gtin, brand, shipping and return policy.
  • AI titles and descriptions written against the live SERP. Drafts await approval, or run on Autopilot.
  • Opportunity grid — traffic × conversion: hidden gem, intent mismatch, defend, prune.
  • Rank tracking (optional DataForSEO, under your spend cap).
  • Redirects and 404s, slug monitor, static sitemap, robots.txt, alt-text filling, EU Omnibus history, hreflang, Local SEO.

Selling more

  • Recommendations — up-sell, cross-sell and same-need alternatives from your real sales patterns.
  • Rails you order by drag-and-drop, block and classic themes, with custom slots.
  • Pricing engine — role and wholesale prices, brand discounts, loyalty tiers, points, free gifts. Stacked, resolved ahead of time.
  • Merchandising — swatches, labels, trust badges, payment logos, galleries, layout builder, custom tabs, one master button style.
  • Lift measurement — the incremental orders and revenue the engine adds.

Cart, checkout, recovery

  • Side cart, sticky add-to-cart, wishlist, back-in-stock waitlist.
  • Quote requests for catalogue shops — an ask-for-a-price card, a quote basket the shopper grows as they browse, and the browsing trail behind each request, booked as valued leads.
  • A premade contact form — shortcode, block or Elementor widget; messages saved, staff emailed, the visitor thanked in their own language.
  • Saved and abandoned carts — share and resume, cookieless restore that survives CDN caching.
  • Checkout tuning — distraction-free checkout with A/B assignment, minimum order, and business-invoice fields.
  • Full block and classic parity.

Reaching customers

  • Audiences — top, lapsed, lookalike, abandoned-cart, reactivation, competition entrants. Recomputed nightly.
  • Automated campaigns — abandoned cart, win-back, birthday, back in stock, post-purchase. Email and web push, quiet hours honoured.
  • Social posts from your catalogue, competitions on any Gravity Form, surveys scored into NPS and voice-of-customer.

Knowing what worked

  • Server-side measurement you own — Meta CAPI, GA4, Google Ads Enhanced Conversions, TikTok Events API. Deduplicated, sent after the order is saved, with a daily safety net.
  • Consent / GDPR CMP — first-party banner, Consent Mode v2, proof-of-consent log, cookie scanner.
  • ROI Wizard — orders, revenue, cost, net, ROAS and ROI by engine, offer, channel, campaign or creative.
  • Ad spend typed, by CSV, or nightly from Google Ads / Meta / TikTok. Conversion goals for non-shops.
  • Insights Chat — ask your shop questions in wp-admin. Customers pseudonymised, no data export.

Running the shop

  • Marketplace order import — Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, eFood, Wolt, Etsy, Amazon → native WooCommerce orders. The catalogue importer runs it in reverse: import products from a marketplace listing in one click.
  • Streaming feeds — ready-made templates for Google Shopping, Facebook, Amazon Inventory Loader, eBay File Exchange, Etsy listings, Skroutz, BestPrice, Shopflix, eMAG, eFood, Wolt and Tolstoy, plus a custom builder.
  • Sixteen couriers — vouchers, labels, COD, tracking, bulk printing, daily closings: ACS, BOX NOW, Courier Center, ELTA, Geniki Taxydromiki, Speedex, DHL, FedEx, UPS, USPS, Royal Mail, Colissimo, BRT, Correos, Sendcloud, plus a manual carrier.
  • Order documents — invoices, packing slips, proformas, credit notes. Singly or merged across a date range.
  • Delivery economics — real break-even free shipping from your carrier costs, per-carrier × zone P&L.
  • Operational intelligence — stock recovery, missing hot sellers, out-of-stock predictor, branch stock, barcode scanning, optional ERP and supplier feed (XML) imports.

The withdrawal button — Directive (EU) 2023/2673

Every EU distance seller must now give consumers a prominent, permanently available button to declare withdrawal electronically.

  • 14 calendar days from delivery, guests included, no reason required, partial withdrawal by item and quantity.
  • Acknowledgement on a durable medium with date and time; cancellation stays distinct from withdrawal.
  • Return vouchers checked by an operator before the customer sees them. Ships disabled.

Content, blocks and regional selling

  • Events with RSVP, FAQ accordions, Store Pages, Food & Beverages option groups, Google reviews, Media Cleanup that quarantines before it deletes.
  • Dozens of server-rendered blocks for stores, products, recommendations, swatches, brands, categories, blog, competitions and events.
  • Regional checkout — COD by country or courier, “from X,XX €” labels before a postcode is entered, per-country payment and shipping rules.

Speed and resilience

  • Pre-computed into flat tables; the storefront reads single cached rows, and a thin front-end runtime plugin (Pro) serves it without the admin half.
  • Self-healing jobs re-arm after updates and stay dormant until used. Tables are never dropped except on explicit uninstall.

Free and Pro

GPLv3 throughout. There are three separate things here, and two of them are called “Pro”.

1. This plugin, free. A complete, working product, not a demo: AI chat and semantic search, the whole SEO engine, pricing and merchandising, the storefront features, measurement and consent, feeds, courier fulfilment, the block library, Ctrl+K and the complete withdrawal button, which is a legal obligation and stays free.

2. A Pro subscription (or the 14-day trial), activated by connecting the site to your Rooster One account. No per-feature keys. It unlocks the Pro screens whose code is already inside this download:

  • Marketplace order import — Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, eFood, Wolt, Etsy, Amazon.
  • Attribution and ROI — dashboard, ROI Wizard, ad-spend connectors, shipping cost against margin.
  • Audiences and campaigns — audience builder, email and web-push flows, social posts, AI-suggested offers.
  • Customer intelligence — customer lookup, surveys, cancellations and returns analysis, chat analytics.
  • Insights Chat, events and competitions, Action Scheduler cleanup.

3. Two companion plugins, included with a Pro subscription and installed separately. A subscription on its own does not put their code on your server, so these screens ask you to install the plugin rather than pretending to work:

  • Rooster One Runtime — serves the storefront, SEO head, sitemap and redirects without loading the admin half. The biggest single speed difference between free and Pro.
  • Rooster One Pro — carries seven engines this download does not contain: supplier invoice scanning, the accounting and ERP connectors (Entersoft, Galaxy, Soft1, Zoho Books, Oxygen), the catalogue importer, the product exchanger, the duplicate-product merge engine, semantic internal linking and the branch stock scanner.

Everything Pro-locked stays visible with an explanation of what it does, and where a screen also needs the Pro plugin it says so before you buy, not after.

Optional integrations

Nothing below is required; each is an opt-in add-on using your own account.

  • Rooster AI credits (rooster.systems) — powers the AI chat, AI SEO copy and Insights Chat via Anthropic Claude and Voyage AI embeddings, with no per-provider API keys to manage.
  • Recommendations service (eshop-optimizer.com) — graph-database up-sell/cross-sell analysis of your order history.
  • DataForSEO — optional keyword rank tracking under a spend cap you set.
  • Ad and measurement platforms — Google Ads, GA4, Meta and TikTok, each independently selectable.
  • Couriers and marketplaces — your own carrier and marketplace accounts, for vouchers and order import.
  • Google Places / Search Console for location data and search performance.

Source code

Every compiled or minified file ships with its source beside it. The block stylesheets (engine/blocks/<block>/style.css and variants/<variant>.css, and the Contact Form block’s variants/panel.css) are compiled with Tailwind CSS 4 from the recipes next to them (style.src.css, variants/<variant>.src.css, variants/panel.src.css) and the token map they import (engine/blocks/theme.css): npx @tailwindcss/cli -i style.src.css -o style.css --minify in the block’s folder rebuilds one. Every *.min.js and *.min.css is minified from the file of the same name without .min. The admin chrome library in lib/rooster-admin ships its sources the same way (assets/src).
sections.installation:
Rooster One needs PHP 8.1 or newer, and MySQL 8.0.21 or MariaDB 10.3 or newer. On an older database server everything works except the analytics reports, and the admin says so.

  1. Install through Plugins → Add New and search for “Rooster One”, or upload the plugin zip to wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it. Nothing changes on your site yet — almost everything ships off by default.
  3. Open Rooster One in the admin menu. The header shows whether your site was read as a shop, a catalogue or a content site; correct it in one click if it is wrong.
  4. Switch on one capability at a time. Each runs alongside your existing tools until you retire them.

Press Ctrl+K on any admin screen to find anything.
sections.faq:
This is an enormous amount of functionality. Am I supposed to use all of it?

No, and nobody does. Everything is off by default. Rooster One installs beside your current SEO plugin, pixel manager and consent tool and changes nothing at all until you switch a piece on. Turning one thing on does not commit you to the next.

The right way in is to pick the single problem that is costing you most right now and switch on only that. Most shops start with recommendations or the AI chat, see what it does for a fortnight, and only then look further. There is no configuration you must complete before anything works.

Why is this one plugin rather than twelve?

Because it is one idea, not twelve features. Rooster One measures your whole business on a schedule — every product, page, customer, order and session, scored into flat tables — and every feature reads those same tables.

That is why the recommendations, the SEO engine, the audiences, the ad ROI and the AI assistant agree with each other instead of each maintaining a private version of the truth. Twelve plugins cannot do that: they would each need their own copy of your catalogue, their own idea of who your best customers are, and their own cron job to build it.

It is also why the plugin gets faster to use as you switch things on rather than slower. The expensive thinking already happened, on a schedule, off your customer’s request. The second feature you enable reads figures the first one already paid for.

How do I find anything in here?

Ctrl+K from anywhere in wp-admin reaches every addressable place in the plugin, pages, tabs and individual panels, searchable by what a thing does rather than by what it is called. All Features lists every one with pinnable favourites, and every page carries a written description of what it is for. If you cannot remember where something lives, you are not expected to.

Can you help me set it up?

Yes. Pro customers get direct support, and there is a support group one click from the top bar in wp-admin for everyone. Beyond support we offer paid set-up and configuration, and further customisation where a shop needs something the plugin does not do out of the box.

Worth saying plainly: the plugin is built for a real shop we run ourselves, so what a working shop needs tends to already be in it, and when it is not, we are the people who can add it. If you would rather hand the configuration to somebody who has done it before, that is a service we sell rather than a favour we occasionally do.

We have our own developers. Can they work with it directly?

Yes, and this is the case we design for rather than tolerate. The plugin is GPLv3, so there is nothing to license and nothing obfuscated. Your team gets 218 filters and 48 actions with the aieo_ prefix covering the parts most likely to need bending, a REST surface, and nine WP-CLI commands for anything that belongs in a deployment script rather than in a browser.

Behaviour is switchable in code as well as in the admin, so a decision your team wants to own can live in your own plugin instead of in our settings table. Where an integration is genuinely missing we would rather add the hook than have you patch the plugin, since a patched copy stops receiving updates. Send us the case.

We are also happy to work alongside an in-house team rather than instead of one: they keep the domain knowledge and the deployment pipeline, we cover the parts of the plugin nobody outside it should have to reverse-engineer.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. Rooster One works on content sites and catalogues too, and adapts what it measures: a content site is scored on visits, engagement and form submissions rather than sales. A badge in the header tells you which of the three it has decided you are, so you are never guessing why a number looks the way it does.

Is the free version crippled?

No. It is a complete product: the AI assistant, the full SEO engine, the whole pricing and merchandising stack, the storefront features, measurement and consent, product feeds and courier fulfilment are all in the free version. Pro adds operational capability, not the basics. The withdrawal button is free as well, because it is a legal obligation for every EU distance seller and charging for it would be a poor thing to do.

What does Pro add?

The operational half: marketplace order import, attribution and ROI, audiences and automated campaigns, web push, customer intelligence, Insights Chat, and events and competitions. Those screens are already in this download and a subscription switches them on. Pro also includes two companion plugins you install separately — Rooster One Runtime, which serves the storefront without loading the admin half and is the biggest single speed difference between free and Pro, and Rooster One Pro, which carries supplier invoice scanning, the accounting and ERP connectors, the catalogue importer, the product exchanger, the duplicate-product merge engine and semantic internal linking.

I started the trial. Why does one screen still say a plugin is missing?

Because two different things are called Pro, and only one of them arrives when you connect. The trial and the subscription grant an entitlement, which unlocks the Pro screens whose code is inside this plugin — AI chat, managed AI credits, attribution, audiences and the rest. Seven features live in the separate Rooster One Pro plugin: invoice scanning, the accounting and ERP connectors, the catalogue importer, the product exchanger, the merge engine, semantic internal linking and the branch stock scanner. An entitlement cannot switch on code that is not on the server, so those screens tell you to install the plugin, which your subscription includes. Install and activate it and they come alive with no further setup.

If my Pro licence lapses, does my storefront change?

No, and that is deliberate. Pro gates the screens where you curate and configure, never the code that draws your shop. The semantic related-content section, the recommendation rails and the policies you have already set keep rendering from what was already worked out, on the free plugin, with no Pro plugin loaded at all. What you lose is the ability to change them: the Duplicate products screen, Semantic Internal Linking and the feed-source generator stop opening, and their controls stop answering. We would rather a lapsed licence cost you the settings screen than blank a live section of your website in front of your customers.

Do I have to pay for AI to use the plugin?

No. The plugin is GPLv3 and a great deal of it — the chat, recommendations, the SEO engine and every storefront and pricing tool — runs without any subscription. Only features that actually call a model consume Rooster AI credits, and the ones that do say so before they run rather than after.

Will it slow my site down?

The design goal is the opposite. Expensive work is pre-computed on a schedule into flat tables, and the storefront reads single cached rows, so enabling a feature adds a feature rather than a per-request query. On Pro the runtime plugin serves the front end without loading the admin half at all.

Will it cope with a large catalogue?

That is what the architecture is for. Heavy analysis runs on a schedule into flat pre-computed tables; the storefront reads single cached rows regardless of how many products sit behind them. Background jobs re-arm themselves after updates, stay dormant until a feature is actually used, and will collapse a runaway third-party task rather than queue politely behind it.

What can the AI chat actually answer?

Questions about your catalogue, grounded in it. It recommends only real, in-stock products and links to them exactly, because it answers from your data rather than from a general model’s memory. You control a knowledge base for the things a catalogue cannot tell it — opening hours, delivery times, returns policy — and identity guardrails stop it describing your business as something it is not.

What happens when the chat does not know something?

It says so, and then tells you. Chat analytics show what was asked, how answers were rated, which questions found nothing, and which conversations ended in an order. The list of questions that found nothing is usually the most valuable screen in the plugin: it is your customers writing your content backlog for you.

Can the chat quote a wrong price?

It reads the same prices the storefront does, including role and wholesale pricing, so a logged-in trade customer and a retail visitor are told different and correct numbers. It is not working from a snapshot taken when the model was trained.

Where does my data go when the AI features run?

Chat runs on Anthropic Claude and semantic search on Voyage AI embeddings. Nothing else leaves your site for those features. Insights Chat, which answers questions about your own shop inside wp-admin, pseudonymises customers and exports no data at all. Every external service the plugin can talk to is listed under “What does Rooster One send to an outside service, and when?” below.

Does semantic search replace the WooCommerce search box?

It can. Semantic search indexes products, posts, pages and terms as embeddings, so “something for dry hair in winter” finds the right products without those words appearing in any title. It runs alongside the built-in search rather than ripping it out, so you can compare before you commit.

How do the recommendations decide what to show?

From what your customers actually did, not from tags you maintain by hand. Up-sells, cross-sells and same-need alternatives are derived from real order history and refreshed on a schedule, so a new product earns its place as soon as it starts selling and a discontinued one leaves without you remembering to remove it.

Can I control where recommendations appear?

Yes. You order the rails by drag and drop, they work on both block and classic themes, and custom slots let you place one anywhere a theme accepts a block. Each rail can be turned off independently, which matters more than it sounds: the commonest cause of a slow product page is four rails nobody asked for.

Can I tell whether the recommendations are actually working?

Yes, and this is the part most plugins leave out. Lift measurement reports the incremental orders and revenue the engine adds, rather than counting every order that happened to contain a recommended product. The second number is always bigger and always flattering, which is presumably why it is the one usually reported.

Can I do wholesale or B2B pricing?

Yes. The pricing engine handles role and wholesale prices, brand-level discounts, loyalty tiers, points and free gifts, and it stacks them in a defined order rather than letting the last filter to run win. Prices are resolved ahead of time into the same pre-computed tables everything else reads, so a complicated rule set does not become a slow product page.

Do you support variation swatches?

Yes, with colour, image and button styles, and they render on archives and product pages from a cache rather than by loading every variation. Alongside them sit labels, trust badges, payment logos, gallery handling, a layout builder, custom tabs, and one master button style so the shop stops looking like four plugins bolted together.

How does abandoned-cart recovery work, and do I need an email service?

Carts are saved server-side, and the restore is cookieless so it survives CDN caching and a customer moving device. Recovery messages go out through automated campaigns by email or web push, using WordPress’s own mail path or your SMTP plugin. You do not need a third-party marketing service, and quiet hours are honoured so nobody is pushed a cart at three in the morning.

What else can the campaigns do?

Win-back, birthday, back-in-stock, post-purchase follow-ups and reactivation, all triggered from the same audience data. Audiences themselves — top customers, lapsed, lookalike, abandoned-cart, reactivation, competition entrants — are recomputed nightly, so a campaign aimed at “lapsed” means lapsed today rather than lapsed whenever the segment was last built by hand.

How are audiences built?

From behaviour the plugin already records, recomputed nightly rather than assembled by hand. The ready-made ones are top customers, lapsed, lookalike, abandoned-cart, reactivation and competition entrants, so “lapsed” means lapsed as of last night rather than lapsed whenever somebody last exported a spreadsheet.

Can I define my own audiences?

Yes. The audience builder takes rules over what customers bought, browsed, abandoned or responded to, combined the way you would say them out loud: ever purchased this brand, not in the last ninety days, opted in. An audience is a live definition, not a frozen list, so it repopulates itself as people move in and out of it.

What can I do with an audience once it exists?

Send it a campaign, target an offer at it, exclude it from another campaign, or push it as a segment for advertising. The same definitions feed the ROI reporting, so you can ask what a segment actually returned rather than only how many people are in it.

Do I need a separate service for web push?

No. Push is served from your own site with its own opt-in gating, and the same quiet-hours rules apply. It is part of the campaign engine rather than a separate product with its own dashboard.

Will it conflict with my current SEO plugin?

No. The SEO engine self-gates behind AIOSEO, Yoast and Rank Math and stays dormant until you explicitly switch it on. There is a read-only importer for all three — page and category settings, site-wide settings and redirect rules — and a head-parity check, so you can compare the output before cutting over, and switch back if you do not like what you see.

What does the SEO engine do that a general SEO plugin does not?

It knows what you sell. Commerce schema is assembled from the same tables the rest of the plugin uses: ProductGroup with hasVariant, per-variant colour, gtin, brand, shipping and return policy. Titles and descriptions are written against the live search results page and wait for your approval, or run on Autopilot if you would rather they did not.

Will I lose rankings if I switch SEO plugins?

That is exactly what the head-parity check exists to answer. It compares what your current plugin emits against what Rooster One would emit, page by page, before anything changes. The importer is read-only, so your existing plugin’s data is never altered, and the engine stays gated until you decide.

Which SEO problems does it actually find?

The opportunity grid plots traffic against conversion and sorts pages into hidden gems, intent mismatches, pages to defend and pages to prune. That is a different question from “what is my score out of a hundred”, and a more useful one. Underneath it sit redirects and 404 monitoring, a slug monitor, a static sitemap, robots.txt, alt-text filling, hreflang, Local SEO, and EU Omnibus price history.

Do you track keyword rankings?

Optionally, through DataForSEO, under a spend cap you set. It is off unless you turn it on and give it your own credentials, because rank tracking is the one part of SEO with a per-query cost and we would rather you decided the size of that bill.

Does it work with the block checkout?

Yes, with full block and classic parity. That is deliberate and tested rather than assumed: the newer block checkout behaves differently enough that features working in one can silently do nothing in the other. Several bugs we have reported upstream to WooCommerce were exactly that shape.

Do I need my own courier accounts?

Yes. The plugin holds sixteen carrier integrations and talks to each with your credentials; it is not a reseller and takes no cut of your shipping. Vouchers, labels, cash on delivery, tracking, bulk printing and daily closings are handled in wp-admin, and a manual carrier covers anyone without an API.

How do I know what free-shipping threshold to set?

Delivery economics computes the real break-even from your actual carrier costs rather than from a round number that felt about right. It also reports profit and loss per carrier and per zone, which usually reveals that one zone has been quietly subsidised by the rest for a long time.

Can I print invoices and packing slips?

Yes: invoices, packing slips, proformas and credit notes, singly or merged across a date range for a whole day’s dispatch. They are generated from the order rather than from a template you keep in sync by hand.

Can I sell on marketplaces from my catalogue?

Both directions. Ready-made feed templates cover the major marketplaces and shopping engines, with a custom builder for anything not on the list, and marketplace orders come back as native WooCommerce orders rather than into a separate silo. The catalogue importer runs the same road in reverse when you want to pull a marketplace listing set in.

Does the measurement replace GA4 and the Meta pixel?

It complements them and makes them survive ad blockers and consent choices. Conversions go server-side to Meta CAPI, GA4, Google Ads Enhanced Conversions and the TikTok Events API, deduplicated against the browser tags you already have, sent after the order is saved so a failed send can never cost you an order, with a daily safety net that re-sends anything that slipped.

How does it handle consent?

A first-party consent banner with Google Consent Mode v2, a proof-of-consent log so you can show what a visitor agreed to and when, and a cookie scanner that reports what your site actually sets rather than what you believe it sets. Measurement respects the answer rather than working around it.

Can I see the return on my ad spend?

The ROI Wizard reports orders, revenue, cost, net, ROAS and ROI by engine, offer, channel, campaign or creative. Ad spend can be typed in, uploaded as CSV, or synced nightly from Google Ads, Meta and TikTok. Shops that do not sell can set conversion goals instead and be measured on those.

Does it suggest what to advertise?

Yes. The composer turns what the shop already knows — your product sets, brands, categories and demand signals — into a complete draft Google Ads campaign, written down in full before anything touches Google’s API. You read the campaign, the ad groups and the actual copy as plain text and decide.

Will it spend my ad budget without asking?

No, and this is the part we would want you to check rather than take on trust. A plan has three states. Draft exists only on your site. Created means it has been pushed to Google Ads and is sitting there paused, real objects spending nothing. Activated means a human enabled it in Google.

Rooster One records that third step. It never performs it. There is no code path in the plugin that turns a campaign on, which is deliberate: composing an advert and committing your money are different decisions and only one of them should be automatable.

What should I write about next?

Ask the customers who already told you. Content gaps are distilled from the storefront chat agent’s own conversations: the questions that returned no products, and the answers customers rated badly, weighted by how often they come up. That turns “what do people keep asking that we answer poorly” into a ranked list of things to write, sourced from demand rather than from a keyword tool’s guess.

It is the loop we are most pleased with in the whole plugin: the chat widget’s failures become the SEO team’s brief.

Can it write social posts for me?

In two steps, kept separate on purpose. First it ranks which of your products and posts are worth promoting, using the same demand scores the SEO engine uses, so you are not promoting whatever happened to be published last. Then, for one object you choose, it drafts platform-native copy for Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn or TikTok.

It only ever drafts. Nothing is published, and no social account tokens are touched by the drafting step. Ranking candidates is free; writing the copy is the part that consumes AI credits.

What is Insights Chat?

Somewhere to ask your shop a question in plain language inside wp-admin, instead of building a report. Customers are pseudonymised and no data is exported. It is the one AI feature aimed at you rather than at your visitors.

What does it do about stock?

Stock recovery finds sales you lost to out-of-stocks, missing-hot-sellers finds products you should be carrying, and an out-of-stock predictor warns you before the shelf empties. There is branch stock for multi-location retail, barcode scanning, and an optional ERP bridge.

What happens to my data if I update or deactivate?

Nothing is removed. Tables are never dropped on update, activation or deactivation — only when you explicitly uninstall the plugin. Deactivating to test something is safe.

Is it translated?

Yes. Admin and storefront are both fully translatable, a complete translation ships with the plugin, and source strings are English and extractable with Poedit.

Does this make my shop compliant with the withdrawal-button law?

It gives you the mechanism Directive (EU) 2023/2673 requires: a permanent, prominent withdrawal button that works for guests, a separate confirmation step, partial withdrawal on multi-item orders, and an email acknowledgement recording the content, date and time of the declaration. That is the part software can do. Every EU member state transposes the Directive into national law, so check the date that applies in your own market.

The rest is yours: your terms of sale, who pays return postage (Directive 2011/83/EU article 14 leaves that partly to your terms), and actually processing the declarations and refunds you receive. The plugin will not pretend those are done because a button exists. The feature ships disabled for that reason — switch it on when your policy is ready.

Is “cancel my order” the same as withdrawal?

No, and treating them as the same is the commonest way a compliant-looking implementation fails. Cancelling an unshipped order is a commercial courtesy you grant on your own terms and may refuse once the parcel has left. Withdrawal is a statutory right exercisable for 14 calendar days from receipt, which you cannot refuse and whose window you do not set. Rooster One keeps them as two separate flows.

What does Rooster One send to an outside service, and when?

Rooster One runs on your own server. It contacts an outside service only in the
cases listed here, and every one of them is either something you switched on or
something you pressed Send on.

rooster.systems — our own service. Privacy policy: https://rooster.systems/privacy/

  • Feedback. When you press Send in the feedback window, we receive your
    message, the category and star rating you chose, the Rooster One screen you
    were on, your site address, an install identifier, and the versions of Rooster
    One, WordPress, WooCommerce and PHP. Your reply address is included unless you
    tick “send anonymously”. Nothing is sent if you close the window.
  • Surveys. When you press Send on the welcome or check-in survey, we receive
    your answers as short codes (never the wording you saw, so every language
    answers can be counted together), your site address, an install identifier, an
    opaque per-person identifier that lets us tell two administrators of the same
    shop apart without telling us who either of them is, the Rooster One version,
    your admin language, and whether the site reports itself as production or
    staging. Your reply address is included only if you leave it in. Closing the
    window sends nothing.
  • Feature usage — Pro and trial only, and off unless you switch it on. A
    weekly report of which Rooster One controls have been used on this site: a
    control name, a screen and a count. Never an order, a customer, a price, or
    anything typed into a field. A free installation schedules no background task
    and makes no request. Turn it off under Rooster One and the schedule is
    removed on the next admin page load.
  • AI credits. If you connect a Rooster account, AI chat, AI SEO copy and
    Insights Chat are served through rooster.systems, which relays them to
    Anthropic (Claude) and Voyage AI. Only the text needed to answer is sent.

No user agent and no browsing history is collected on any of these paths, and
none of them runs on your storefront — they are admin-only, and the first two
happen only when a human presses a button.

Store maps. The Store Map block shows a store’s location from OpenStreetMap
(https://www.openstreetmap.org; terms https://wiki.osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use,
privacy https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy), or from Google Maps
(https://maps.google.com; terms https://policies.google.com/terms, privacy
https://policies.google.com/privacy) where a Google key is configured or the block
is set to it. The map loads in the visitor’s browser only when it comes into view
after the visitor’s first scroll, tap or key press, or when they press “Show the
map”; their browser then requests the map for the store’s coordinates from that
service. The “Get directions” and “View larger map” links open Google Maps or
OpenStreetMap only when pressed.

Other services are listed under Optional integrations above; each is off until
you supply your own account details for it.

How is personal data handled?

For WooCommerce stores, product recommendations are produced by our graph-database service at https://eshop-optimizer.com. It is privacy-centric: you can opt out of sharing product and category names and prices with limited impact on quality, and withhold customer IDs for anonymity. Oxford Metadata Ltd maintains privacy provisions approved by both Google and Facebook — see https://eshop-optimizer.com/compliance.

Hashed PII is never stored or logged raw. Customers are pseudonymised in Insights Chat. Consent is recorded with an IP/UA-hashed proof-of-consent audit log.

short_description: SEO, recommendations, pricing, pixels, couriers, feeds, wishlist, AI chat: 581 tools replacing dozens of plugins. One to load, and they agree.
description:
One plugin instead of dozens. 581 tools, and they agree with each other.

Rooster One does the work that would otherwise take dozens of separate plugins, and it does it from one place, on one set of numbers.

One plugin means one licence, one update, one place to ask, and one thing for WordPress to load on every request instead of dozens.

What is actually in it: a full SEO engine that can take over from Yoast or AIOSEO, importing what they hold first. Product recommendations built from your real sales. Role, wholesale and tiered pricing. Meta, Google Ads, GA4 and TikTok measurement, sent server-side so an ad blocker cannot silence it. Sixteen couriers with vouchers, labels, tracking and daily closings. Marketplace feeds and order import for Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, Etsy, Amazon and more. Side cart, wishlist, back-in-stock waitlist, quote requests for catalogue shops, swatches, trust badges. Popups and scheduled announcements. Abandoned-cart recovery, email and web push campaigns, audiences. Surveys, competitions and events. Invoices, packing slips and credit notes. A GDPR consent banner with a cookie scanner. The EU withdrawal button that Directive 2023/2673 now requires. And an AI assistant that answers from your own catalogue rather than making things up.

That is 581 tools, each with a written description of what it is for.

Why one plugin rather than dozens

Because separate plugins cannot see what the others know, so they disagree, and each one works the same thing out again while your customer waits.

Rooster One measures your whole business on a schedule instead: every product, page, customer, order and session, written into flat tables. The SEO engine, the recommendations, the audiences, the ad ROI report and the AI assistant all read those same tables. That is why they agree, and why the plugin gets faster as you switch more of it on: the heavy work happened before the request arrived. The trade-off is timing: a figure is only as new as its last run.

And it is one plugin to load, not dozens

WordPress loads every active plugin on every request, whether that request needs it or not; a site carrying a hundred of them pays that toll a hundred times before any useful work happens. Rooster One is one plugin, and the parts you have not switched on register nothing. On Pro, a separate lightweight runtime serves the storefront, so your customer’s page load carries the code that draws the page and not the code that runs the shop.

Everything is off by default. It installs beside your current SEO plugin, pixel manager and consent tool and changes nothing until you switch a piece on.

Rooster One runs on your own server. Everything it ever sends to an outside service, and what triggers it, is listed under “What does Rooster One send to an outside service, and when?” in the FAQ below.

The free version is a complete product, not a demo: 775 of the 1,302 screens, tools and actions are in it. Pro adds the operational half and the separate front-end runtime plugin.

Who builds it

Rooster One is built by Oxford Metadata Ltd, approved under Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program for security work; the plugin’s bot filtering, form captcha, proof-of-consent log and login hardening come out of that discipline. The AI features run on Anthropic Claude and Voyage AI embeddings.

It reads your site for what it is

  • Shop — sales and add-to-carts are the measure.
  • Catalogue — products published but not sold; engagement is the measure.
  • Content — no WooCommerce; visits, engagement and forms are the measure.

Auto-detected, overridable in one click. Scoring, cornerstones and applicable signals all follow from it.

You can find all of it

Ctrl+K reaches every page and each of the 581 tools inside them. All Features lists every one, with pinnable favourites, and prints the figure for your own install, since the page count depends on which modules apply to your shop.

What gets measured

Computed on a schedule, stored flat. Everything below reads these.

  • Product vitals — velocity, out-of-stock history, price history, basket role, returns, and a 0–100 demand score.
  • Content vitals — reach, engagement, freshness and a content-demand score for every post, page and custom type.
  • Customer vitals — an omnichannel profile: purchases, affinities, lifecycle stage, survey answers, return risk.
  • Session and attribution rollups — engagement joined to conversion on one session id, with landing page, campaign and five UTMs.
  • Effective prices — every price rule resolved ahead of time into one row per product per audience.

The features

AI chat & semantic search

  • Chat widget on Anthropic Claude, grounded in your catalogue — only real, in-stock items with exact links.
  • Semantic search on Voyage AI embeddings across products, posts, pages and terms.
  • A knowledge base you control, with identity guardrails so it cannot mis-describe you.
  • Chat analytics — what was asked, how it was rated, which questions found nothing, which chats ended in an order.
  • Related content on articles, guides, listings and products, from the same index, automatic or placed by block or shortcode.

SEO engine

Imports from, and can take over from, AIOSEO, Yoast or Rank Math; stays gated behind your current SEO plugin until you switch over.

  • Head, canonical, robots, Open Graph, Twitter and JSON-LD, assembled once into a cache.
  • Commerce schema from the same tables — ProductGroup + hasVariant, per-variant colour, gtin, brand, shipping and return policy.
  • AI titles and descriptions written against the live SERP. Drafts await approval, or run on Autopilot.
  • Opportunity grid — traffic × conversion: hidden gem, intent mismatch, defend, prune.
  • Rank tracking (optional DataForSEO, under your spend cap).
  • Redirects and 404s, slug monitor, static sitemap, robots.txt, alt-text filling, EU Omnibus history, hreflang, Local SEO.

Selling more

  • Recommendations — up-sell, cross-sell and same-need alternatives from your real sales patterns.
  • Rails you order by drag-and-drop, block and classic themes, with custom slots.
  • Pricing engine — role and wholesale prices, brand discounts, loyalty tiers, points, free gifts. Stacked, resolved ahead of time.
  • Merchandising — swatches, labels, trust badges, payment logos, galleries, layout builder, custom tabs, one master button style.
  • Lift measurement — the incremental orders and revenue the engine adds.

Cart, checkout, recovery

  • Side cart, sticky add-to-cart, wishlist, back-in-stock waitlist.
  • Quote requests for catalogue shops — an ask-for-a-price card, a quote basket the shopper grows as they browse, and the browsing trail behind each request, booked as valued leads.
  • A premade contact form — shortcode, block or Elementor widget; messages saved, staff emailed, the visitor thanked in their own language.
  • Saved and abandoned carts — share and resume, cookieless restore that survives CDN caching.
  • Checkout tuning — distraction-free checkout with A/B assignment, minimum order, and business-invoice fields.
  • Full block and classic parity.

Reaching customers

  • Audiences — top, lapsed, lookalike, abandoned-cart, reactivation, competition entrants. Recomputed nightly.
  • Automated campaigns — abandoned cart, win-back, birthday, back in stock, post-purchase. Email and web push, quiet hours honoured.
  • Social posts from your catalogue, competitions on any Gravity Form, surveys scored into NPS and voice-of-customer.

Knowing what worked

  • Server-side measurement you own — Meta CAPI, GA4, Google Ads Enhanced Conversions, TikTok Events API. Deduplicated, sent after the order is saved, with a daily safety net.
  • Consent / GDPR CMP — first-party banner, Consent Mode v2, proof-of-consent log, cookie scanner.
  • ROI Wizard — orders, revenue, cost, net, ROAS and ROI by engine, offer, channel, campaign or creative.
  • Ad spend typed, by CSV, or nightly from Google Ads / Meta / TikTok. Conversion goals for non-shops.
  • Insights Chat — ask your shop questions in wp-admin. Customers pseudonymised, no data export.

Running the shop

  • Marketplace order import — Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, eFood, Wolt, Etsy, Amazon → native WooCommerce orders. The catalogue importer runs it in reverse: import products from a marketplace listing in one click.
  • Streaming feeds — ready-made templates for Google Shopping, Facebook, Amazon Inventory Loader, eBay File Exchange, Etsy listings, Skroutz, BestPrice, Shopflix, eMAG, eFood, Wolt and Tolstoy, plus a custom builder.
  • Sixteen couriers — vouchers, labels, COD, tracking, bulk printing, daily closings: ACS, BOX NOW, Courier Center, ELTA, Geniki Taxydromiki, Speedex, DHL, FedEx, UPS, USPS, Royal Mail, Colissimo, BRT, Correos, Sendcloud, plus a manual carrier.
  • Order documents — invoices, packing slips, proformas, credit notes. Singly or merged across a date range.
  • Delivery economics — real break-even free shipping from your carrier costs, per-carrier × zone P&L.
  • Operational intelligence — stock recovery, missing hot sellers, out-of-stock predictor, branch stock, barcode scanning, optional ERP and supplier feed (XML) imports.

The withdrawal button — Directive (EU) 2023/2673

Every EU distance seller must now give consumers a prominent, permanently available button to declare withdrawal electronically.

  • 14 calendar days from delivery, guests included, no reason required, partial withdrawal by item and quantity.
  • Acknowledgement on a durable medium with date and time; cancellation stays distinct from withdrawal.
  • Return vouchers checked by an operator before the customer sees them. Ships disabled.

Content, blocks and regional selling

  • Events with RSVP, FAQ accordions, Store Pages, Food & Beverages option groups, Google reviews, Media Cleanup that quarantines before it deletes.
  • Dozens of server-rendered blocks for stores, products, recommendations, swatches, brands, categories, blog, competitions and events.
  • Regional checkout — COD by country or courier, “from X,XX €” labels before a postcode is entered, per-country payment and shipping rules.

Speed and resilience

  • Pre-computed into flat tables; the storefront reads single cached rows, and a thin front-end runtime plugin (Pro) serves it without the admin half.
  • Self-healing jobs re-arm after updates and stay dormant until used. Tables are never dropped except on explicit uninstall.

Free and Pro

GPLv3 throughout. There are three separate things here, and two of them are called “Pro”.

1. This plugin, free. A complete, working product, not a demo: AI chat and semantic search, the whole SEO engine, pricing and merchandising, the storefront features, measurement and consent, feeds, courier fulfilment, the block library, Ctrl+K and the complete withdrawal button, which is a legal obligation and stays free.

2. A Pro subscription (or the 14-day trial), activated by connecting the site to your Rooster One account. No per-feature keys. It unlocks the Pro screens whose code is already inside this download:

  • Marketplace order import — Skroutz, Shopflix, eMAG, eFood, Wolt, Etsy, Amazon.
  • Attribution and ROI — dashboard, ROI Wizard, ad-spend connectors, shipping cost against margin.
  • Audiences and campaigns — audience builder, email and web-push flows, social posts, AI-suggested offers.
  • Customer intelligence — customer lookup, surveys, cancellations and returns analysis, chat analytics.
  • Insights Chat, events and competitions, Action Scheduler cleanup.

3. Two companion plugins, included with a Pro subscription and installed separately. A subscription on its own does not put their code on your server, so these screens ask you to install the plugin rather than pretending to work:

  • Rooster One Runtime — serves the storefront, SEO head, sitemap and redirects without loading the admin half. The biggest single speed difference between free and Pro.
  • Rooster One Pro — carries seven engines this download does not contain: supplier invoice scanning, the accounting and ERP connectors (Entersoft, Galaxy, Soft1, Zoho Books, Oxygen), the catalogue importer, the product exchanger, the duplicate-product merge engine, semantic internal linking and the branch stock scanner.

Everything Pro-locked stays visible with an explanation of what it does, and where a screen also needs the Pro plugin it says so before you buy, not after.

Optional integrations

Nothing below is required; each is an opt-in add-on using your own account.

  • Rooster AI credits (rooster.systems) — powers the AI chat, AI SEO copy and Insights Chat via Anthropic Claude and Voyage AI embeddings, with no per-provider API keys to manage.
  • Recommendations service (eshop-optimizer.com) — graph-database up-sell/cross-sell analysis of your order history.
  • DataForSEO — optional keyword rank tracking under a spend cap you set.
  • Ad and measurement platforms — Google Ads, GA4, Meta and TikTok, each independently selectable.
  • Couriers and marketplaces — your own carrier and marketplace accounts, for vouchers and order import.
  • Google Places / Search Console for location data and search performance.

Source code

Every compiled or minified file ships with its source beside it. The block stylesheets (engine/blocks/<block>/style.css and variants/<variant>.css, and the Contact Form block’s variants/panel.css) are compiled with Tailwind CSS 4 from the recipes next to them (style.src.css, variants/<variant>.src.css, variants/panel.src.css) and the token map they import (engine/blocks/theme.css): npx @tailwindcss/cli -i style.src.css -o style.css --minify in the block’s folder rebuilds one. Every *.min.js and *.min.css is minified from the file of the same name without .min. The admin chrome library in lib/rooster-admin ships its sources the same way (assets/src).

aieo/post-related-needs.name: aieo/post-related-needs
aieo/post-related-needs.title: Rooster One Post Related Needs
aieo/post-related-needs.description: Need-tag chips for the current blog post. Reads wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations for pa_need → post edges. Each chip links to the need archive. With include (a list of taxonomies) it shows the post's other links too: its product categories, needs and brands, and its own tags (post_tag). Display row: one row of chips at the start, the post's foot.

aieo/lowest-price-message.name: aieo/lowest-price-message
aieo/lowest-price-message.title: Rooster One Lowest Price Message
aieo/lowest-price-message.description: EU Omnibus: on on-sale products, shows the operator-configured message with the lowest price before the reduction. Auto-hides when the product is not on sale.

aieo/recos.name: aieo/recos
aieo/recos.title: Rooster One Recommendations
aieo/recos.description: Renders one Rooster One recommendation surface (same_needs / crosssells / upsells / related / recently_viewed / semantic_related) as the placeholder div the lazy-recommendations.js bundle hydrator picks up on first user interaction. Same emitted markup as the legacy inline `<div id="aieo-X-placeholder">` blocks so the existing JS hydrator works unchanged.

aieo/post-related-brands.name: aieo/post-related-brands
aieo/post-related-brands.title: Rooster One Post Related Brands
aieo/post-related-brands.description: Brand-logo slider for the current blog post. Reads wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations for product_brand → post edges.

aieo/popup-panel.name: aieo/popup-panel
aieo/popup-panel.title: Rooster One Popup Panel
aieo/popup-panel.description: The split layout for a popup: a content pane you fill with any blocks, and a full-bleed image pane that sits beside it on desktop and moves above it on mobile — with a separate mobile image so a landscape photo never gets cropped to nothing on a phone. Built for the aieo_popup post type, but usable inline on any page.

aieo/competition.name: aieo/competition
aieo/competition.title: Competition
aieo/competition.description: Renders a competition — hero image, title, short description, the entry form and share buttons. Auto-binds to the competition page it's placed on, or pick a specific competition.

aieo/product-needs.name: aieo/product-needs
aieo/product-needs.title: Rooster One Product Needs
aieo/product-needs.description: Renders the 'This product covers:' Επιθυμίες (needs) list for the current single-product page. Wraps the existing AIEO_DMM_Product_Needs renderer so non-block themes keep their PHP path; on a block-themed PDP this is the canonical entry. Reads from `wp_aieo_dmm_product_needs` and `pa_need` taxonomy.

aieo/post-related-categories.name: aieo/post-related-categories
aieo/post-related-categories.title: Rooster One Post Related Product Categories
aieo/post-related-categories.description: Dropdown of related product categories for the current blog post. Reads wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations for product_cat → post edges.

aieo/contact-form.name: aieo/contact-form
aieo/contact-form.title: Contact Form
aieo/contact-form.description: The Rooster One contact form: saves every message, notifies your staff and thanks the visitor by email. Choose the fields, which are required and the layout per placement; the defaults live under Rooster One > Contact Form. Or choose the Panel look to place one of your own forms (Rooster One's forms, their fields and layout yours) in a landing's form panel.

aieo/free-shipping-pdp.name: aieo/free-shipping-pdp
aieo/free-shipping-pdp.title: Rooster One Free Shipping (PDP bar)
aieo/free-shipping-pdp.description: Per-product free-shipping progress bar. Reads threshold + messages + appearance from AIEO_DMM_Free_Shipping (admin: DMM → Free Shipping + COD) and the current cart subtotal from WC()->cart. Self-hides when the operator's `display_product` setting is off, when the threshold is 0, when the product is on the no-free-shipping exclusion list, or when the cart is empty AND the operator chose to suppress the empty-cart message. Updates client-side on every cart change via a tiny REST poll.

aieo/post-meta.name: aieo/post-meta
aieo/post-meta.title: Rooster One Product Post Meta (SKU + Barcodes)
aieo/post-meta.description: Renders the SKU + per-variation barcode rows for the current product. Wraps AIEO_DMM_Product_Meta — the same module the `[om_ppe_product_meta]` shortcode uses (admin-configurable via DMM settings: show_sku, show_barcode, label customisation). On variable products the barcode row expands to one barcode per variation, hidden behind a `+ more` toggle.

aieo/product-variations-gallery.name: aieo/product-variations-gallery
aieo/product-variations-gallery.title: Rooster One Product Variations Gallery
aieo/product-variations-gallery.description: Variation-aware product gallery: when a shopper selects a variation, the main product image and its gallery swap in place to that variation's own images. Reads each variation's existing image set, so there is no data migration.

aieo/product-slider.name: aieo/product-slider
aieo/product-slider.title: Rooster One Product Slider
aieo/product-slider.description: A horizontal product slider with the SAME look as the product-page recommendations (thin uppercase title + line, then cards). Set the title manually and pick products by category, tag and/or specific product IDs, or show the products of the post it is placed with (source: post). Layout list: one compact row per product (picture, brand, name, price), the post's «Shop the story».

aieo/favourite.name: aieo/favourite
aieo/favourite.title: Rooster One Favourite
aieo/favourite.description: The heart of a brand, a product category, a need or a blog post: keeps it in the visitor's favourites (the same list as Favourites in the account and the side cart). Without an item set, the post in context or the archive's term.

aieo/brand-archive-hero.name: aieo/brand-archive-hero
aieo/brand-archive-hero.title: Rooster One Brand Archive Hero
aieo/brand-archive-hero.description: Per-brand hero for the brand archive (taxonomy-product_brand). Reads queried brand term, joins core_brand_vitals + dmm_brand_extras. Renders hero image, logo overlay, headline, product count, wishlist heart, rating stars.

aieo/custom-slots-region.name: aieo/custom-slots-region
aieo/custom-slots-region.title: Rooster One Custom Slots Region
aieo/custom-slots-region.description: Placeholder block that, at render time, enumerates every enabled slot from the Custom Slots admin store and emits each as a sibling div. Designed to sit inside the .ff-recommendations-cluster flex container so each slot participates in the Recommendations Ordering CSS (`order:` / `display:none`) alongside the built-in aieo/recos rails. This block emits NO wrapper of its own — slot divs are direct flex children of the parent group.

aieo/breadcrumb.name: aieo/breadcrumb
aieo/breadcrumb.title: Rooster One Breadcrumb
aieo/breadcrumb.description: SEO-consistent breadcrumb. Uses the SAME pinned canonical category as Rooster One's canonical URL and JSON-LD BreadcrumbList, so the visible trail never disagrees with what Google reads.

aieo/brand-slider.name: aieo/brand-slider
aieo/brand-slider.title: Rooster One Brand Slider
aieo/brand-slider.description: Brand carousel. Modes: top, new_brand, new_product, favourites (per-user affinity), manual. Server-renders the cards as a scroll-snap row in the theme's look (on Rooster Zero the theme's card surface and motion); arrows on pointer screens, a swiped strip on phones.

aieo/sale-eligibility-message.name: aieo/sale-eligibility-message
aieo/sale-eligibility-message.title: Rooster One Sale Eligibility Message
aieo/sale-eligibility-message.description: Conditional badge that appears under the price WHEN the current product is on sale, telling the shopper how they qualify for the sale price (everyone, signed-in only, PRO role, etc.). Auto-hides on non-sale products. Token replacement: {regular_price}, {sale_price}, {savings_amount}, {savings_pct}, {role}.

aieo/form-button.name: aieo/form-button
aieo/form-button.title: Form Button
aieo/form-button.description: A button that asks for one of your forms: it opens the form in a window, or goes to the page that holds it. Its words and what it opens are the form's own (Rooster One > Forms, the form's Button box); a placement may change them.

aieo/toc.name: aieo/toc
aieo/toc.title: Rooster One Table of Contents
aieo/toc.description: A table of contents built from the headings of the post being displayed. Works in the post content, in a sidebar or in a block-theme template part; headings without an id get one, headings with an id keep it. Also available as the [aieo_toc] shortcode and as an Elementor widget. Layout inline: the title in small capitals between two rules, the sections as underlined links in one row (the Aurenne text page's «On this page»).

aieo/taxonomy-archive-hero.name: aieo/taxonomy-archive-hero
aieo/taxonomy-archive-hero.title: Rooster One Taxonomy Archive Hero
aieo/taxonomy-archive-hero.description: Generic per-term archive hero. Auto-detects queried taxonomy (product_brand / pa_need / product_tag / product_cat) and dispatches to the right data source — brand vitals + extras for product_brand, need_extras for pa_need, term thumbnail + description for product_tag, category extras for product_cat. Filterable via aieo_taxonomy_archive_hero_data for new taxonomies.

aieo/custom-slot.name: aieo/custom-slot
aieo/custom-slot.title: Rooster One Custom Slot
aieo/custom-slot.description: Renders one operator-defined slot (Tolstoy widget OR free-form HTML/code) from the Custom Slots admin store. Used inside the single-product recommendations cluster so each slot can be drag-positioned alongside the built-in reco rails. Resolve target via slotId.

aieo/loyalty-connection.name: aieo/loyalty-connection
aieo/loyalty-connection.title: Rooster One Loyalty Connection
aieo/loyalty-connection.description: Bonus-card loyalty — connect/identify, then show the most recent points.

aieo/taxonomy-archive-footer.name: aieo/taxonomy-archive-footer
aieo/taxonomy-archive-footer.title: Rooster One Taxonomy Archive Footer
aieo/taxonomy-archive-footer.description: Per-term editorial / SEO footer copy. Reads the queried taxonomy's *_extras table footer column when present (need_extras.footer_text, brand_extras.footer_text, category_extras.footer_text). Emits nothing when no footer copy exists for the term.

aieo/event-registration.name: aieo/event-registration
aieo/event-registration.title: Event Registration
aieo/event-registration.description: A self-registration form for an event — guests sign up by email and are taken to their RSVP page. Auto-binds to the event it's placed on, or pick a specific event.

aieo/brand-story.name: aieo/brand-story
aieo/brand-story.title: Rooster One Brand Story
aieo/brand-story.description: Renders brand long-form copy (history, ambassadors, importer, footer) on the brand archive page. Reads queried brand term + wp_aieo_dmm_brand_extras. Emits nothing for sections with no copy.

aieo/taxonomy-related-articles.name: aieo/taxonomy-related-articles
aieo/taxonomy-related-articles.title: Rooster One Taxonomy Related Articles
aieo/taxonomy-related-articles.description: Renders 'From the Blog' article cards related to the queried term — works for any taxonomy (product_cat, pa_need, product_tag, supplier, custom). Reads bidirectional edges from wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations (the same source brand-related uses for product_brand). On the brand archive itself, prefer aieo/brand-related — this block is for the OTHER taxonomies.

aieo/product-card-swatches.name: aieo/product-card-swatches
aieo/product-card-swatches.title: Rooster One Product Swatches
aieo/product-card-swatches.description: Variation swatches for a product. Inside a block product loop it picks up the current product automatically; anywhere else, set a product ID. Renders the same cached swatch HTML every other placement uses.

aieo/brand-related.name: aieo/brand-related
aieo/brand-related.title: Rooster One Brand Related
aieo/brand-related.description: Cross-link strip for the brand archive: related product categories (chips), related blog articles (3-card row), and 'other brands you love' for logged-in viewers. Reads wp_aieo_dmm_term_relations + customer brand affinity.

aieo/latest-posts-overlay.name: aieo/latest-posts-overlay
aieo/latest-posts-overlay.title: Rooster One Latest Posts Overlay
aieo/latest-posts-overlay.description: The latest blog posts as cards on their pictures. The journal (the default): a head with its title and "All stories", then a row of cards, each the picture under the theme's photo scrim with the category and the title over it, a row that swipes on a tablet and a phone. The overlay and the glass looks: a grid with a category badge, a slider on a phone.

aieo/brand-rails.name: aieo/brand-rails
aieo/brand-rails.title: Rooster One Brand Rails
aieo/brand-rails.description: Stacked curated brand rails (Featured / New / Your Favourites / Top). Each rail has its own count and slides-per-view, configurable in the inspector.

aieo/professional-signup.name: aieo/professional-signup
aieo/professional-signup.title: Rooster One Professional Signup
aieo/professional-signup.description: A professional or student account application: the site's own form, approved on its Answers, or Gravity Forms. With filter role-price, the shop filters' PRO only switch.

aieo/semantic-related.name: aieo/semantic-related
aieo/semantic-related.title: Rooster One Related content
aieo/semantic-related.description: Related articles, guides and products, chosen by the semantic engine.

aieo/brand-azindex.name: aieo/brand-azindex
aieo/brand-azindex.title: Rooster One Brand A-Z Index
aieo/brand-azindex.description: Server-rendered A-Z brand directory. Every letter A–Z (plus '#' for non-Latin brands) is always present; empty letters render disabled. Sticky letter bar + per-letter brand grid with product counts. Reads exclusively from wp_aieo_core_brand_vitals.

aieo/store-locator.name: aieo/store-locator
aieo/store-locator.title: Rooster One Store Locator
aieo/store-locator.description: Grid or list of all your store locations — address, phone, opening hours and Google Maps / review links.

aieo/opening-hours.name: aieo/opening-hours
aieo/opening-hours.title: Rooster One Opening Hours
aieo/opening-hours.description: A store location's opening hours. Auto-resolves on a store page, or set a location slug.

aieo/store-map.name: aieo/store-map
aieo/store-map.title: Rooster One Store Map
aieo/store-map.description: A single store's location map (OpenStreetMap, or Google Maps where a Google key is configured) plus a directions link. Auto-resolves on a store page, or set a location slug.

aieo/business-info.name: aieo/business-info
aieo/business-info.title: Rooster One Business Info
aieo/business-info.description: A store location's address, phone, opening hours and Google links — from your Locations & Reviews data.

aieo/google-reviews.name: aieo/google-reviews
aieo/google-reviews.title: Rooster One Google Reviews
aieo/google-reviews.description: Live Google reviews pulled from the local cache. Single location, mixed feed, or cards grid.

aieo/store-hero.name: aieo/store-hero
aieo/store-hero.title: Rooster One Store Hero
aieo/store-hero.description: Shop-page header hero in the category-hero style (centred image, title, horizontal line). Listing title, heading and description come from the bound location. Auto-resolves on a store page, or set a location slug.

aieo/store-info.name: aieo/store-info
aieo/store-info.title: Rooster One Store Info (address, phone, hours)
aieo/store-info.description: Structured store contact info — address, clickable phone, and per-day hours. Reads from post meta + the linked Google location row.

aieo/category-lead.name: aieo/category-lead
aieo/category-lead.title: Rooster One Category Lead
aieo/category-lead.description: The current category's description, falling back to its name when it has none. For blog category archive headers.

aieo/blog-hero.name: aieo/blog-hero
aieo/blog-hero.title: Rooster One Blog Hero (Latest Post)
aieo/blog-hero.description: Featured latest-post hero with the category-hero look: a top title, the newest post's title as the headline, its excerpt as the description and its featured image — all clickable. On a blog category/tag archive it features that term's latest post.

aieo/category-hero.name: aieo/category-hero
aieo/category-hero.title: Rooster One Category Hero
aieo/category-hero.description: The queried category's hero — image, title and description — auto-filled from the term, for product or blog category archive headers.

aieo/blog-subcategories.name: aieo/blog-subcategories
aieo/blog-subcategories.title: Rooster One Blog Subcategories (Dropdown)
aieo/blog-subcategories.description: A dropdown of the current blog category's subcategories, styled like the blog-post categories dropdown. Renders nothing when the category has none.

aieo/page-hero.name: aieo/page-hero
aieo/page-hero.title: Rooster One Page Hero
aieo/page-hero.description: Manual hero — top title, left headline, right description and desktop/mobile images. Identical look to the category hero, usable on any page.

aieo/category-footer-hero.name: aieo/category-footer-hero
aieo/category-footer-hero.title: Rooster One Category Footer Hero
aieo/category-footer-hero.description: The category's SEO footer text beside the category image (image left, rich text right) with the hero divider line. Auto-fills from the queried product category.

aieo/category-chips.name: aieo/category-chips
aieo/category-chips.title: Rooster One Category Chips
aieo/category-chips.description: A row of clickable category chips for the current archive — the term's child categories.
